questions.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{4}{{x}^{2}+1} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{\frac{4}{{x}^{2}}}{\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{\frac{4}{{x}^{2}}}{1+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{0}{1+0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ for $x<0$ with $f(x)=\frac{|3x+6|}{x-4}?$
questions.worked_solution:
For large negative values of $x,$ we have $|3x+6|=-(3x+6).$ Consequently, for $x\to -\infty ,$ we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{|3x+6|}{x-4}={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(3x+6)}{x-4}.
$$

The horizontal asymptote for $x<0$ is $y={lim}_{x\to -\infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(3x+6)}{x-4} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(\frac{3x}{x}+\frac{6}{x})}{(\frac{x}{x}-\frac{4}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(3+\frac{6}{x})}{(1-\frac{4}{x})} \\  & =\frac{-(3+0)}{1-0} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote is $y=-3.$

The horizontal asymptote is $y=\lim_\limits{x \rightarrow \infty} f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x^3.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{5}-10}{{x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{{x}^{5}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{10}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{8{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{({x}^{2}-\frac{10}{{x}^{3}})}{(1-\frac{8}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(\frac{{x}^{2}-0}{1-0}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{2} \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.
